title: Mini project: the shop's best-seller report

steps.title: Report 1: the top 5 best-sellers
steps.prompt:
Time to fly without a net. The boss wants the five best-selling products by quantity sold.
You'll need: a JOIN (products × sale_items), SUM(quantity), GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT p.name, sum(si.quantity) AS sold FROM products p JOIN sale_items si ON si.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY sold DESC LIMIT 5;
hints: Join products p with sale_items si on product_id.
GROUP BY p.name, then ORDER BY sold DESC.
LIMIT 5 finishes - the top row is Mini Tagine, 11 sold.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, sum(si.quantity) AS sold FROM products p JOIN sale_items si ON si.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY sold DESC LIMIT 5;
steps.memory_trick: Project recipe: JOIN → SUM → GROUP → ORDER → LIMIT.

steps.title: Report 2: customers knocking, no one home
steps.prompt:
The boss wants to reward loyal customers and gently re-engage the quiet ones.
Find every customer with zero sales. (LEFT JOIN • IS NULL)
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id WHERE s.id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name;
hints: Keep s.id IS NULL - sales that never happened.
ORDER BY c.name makes the list tidy.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id WHERE s.id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name;
steps.memory_trick: LEFT JOIN + WHERE … IS NULL = 'the lonely ones'.

steps.title: Report 3: how much each category earns
steps.prompt: Finally - money per category. Sale items carry unit_price and quantity; their product knows its category. That's a two-hop JOIN.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT c.name AS category, sum(si.unit_price * si.quantity) AS revenue FROM sale_items si JOIN products p ON p.id = si.product_id JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY revenue DESC;
hints: Join p on p.id = si.product_id; join c on c.id = p.category_id.
Group by c.name, order by revenue DESC.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT c.name AS category, sum(si.unit_price * si.quantity) AS revenue FROM sale_items si JOIN products p ON p.id = si.product_id JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY revenue DESC;

steps.title: Project debrief
steps.prompt:
You just ran a real business report: best-sellers, quiet customers, and category revenue.
Every piece was built from small lessons: SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT.
That's the whole secret - big queries are just small queries glued with new words.
steps.task: Which building block did Report 1 use to rank products?
hints: DESC puts the biggest on top.
The sort clause comes after GROUP BY.
steps.memory_trick: You're not memorising SQL - you're assembling it.
